title: Alaska Winter 2-1: Non-destructive winter landscape post-processing in Photoshop and Camera Raw

locations.name: Alaska (probable, inferred from filename/path)
locations.basis: Filename and folder indicate Alaska winter project; transcript contains no explicit shooting location.

summary: The video presents a hands-on workflow for post-processing winter landscape photography, focusing on snowy scenes, in-camera RAW adjustments, and Photoshop techniques. The instructor emphasizes non-destructive methods, highlights proper exposure for snow, and demonstrates how to recover shadow detail, remove unwanted elements, and craft depth and mood through color grading, fog/distance effects, and careful framing. Key techniques include camera raw whites/shadows adjustments, the clone stamp and healing tools for object removal, the history paint workflow for non-destructive edits, sky-to-foreground color grading with luminosity masking, fog layering to enhance depth, and deliberate cropping and vignette usage to guide the viewer’s eye toward the light source. The session also covers practical tips for consistency of grain, edge handling, and the role of framing in winter imagery, culminating in a mindset of keeping edits simple and print-focused."
topics: Snow exposure management in high-contrast scenes
Bracketing versus exposure balancing in snowy landscapes
Camera Raw: whites, exposure, shadows, and blacks adjustments
Non-destructive editing: history paint workflow in Photoshop
Clone Stamp, Healing Brush, and Remove Tool for removing subjects
Color grading: color temperature, luminosity, and selective color
Sky foreground balance and the use of color grading for mood
Three-zone processing: foreground texture, lighting beam, and sky
Edge framing, composition, and cropping decisions
Fog layering, dehaze, and depth with mist effects
Focus stacking and bracketed shots for dynamic range
Vignettes and localized adjustments to guide viewer attention

sections.title: Snow exposure decisions and bracket cautions
sections.description: Intro to how bright snow can fool bracketed exposure; emphasis on finding a proper middle ground to preserve highlights and recover shadows in Camera Raw.

sections.title: Camera Raw: revealing shadow detail and highlight control
sections.description: Discussion of exposing for snow scenes, pulling down shadows, and recovering detail with 1.9 stops (up to ~3.0) without introducing excessive noise.

sections.title: Horizon and depth in forest composition
sections.description: Guidance on placing trees at varying depths on the horizon to create perceived depth and avoid flat compositions.

sections.title: Framing corrections and edge avoidance
concepts: Positioning and minor moves to fix composition
sections.description: Notes on ensuring the frame doesn’t cut important elements and how small adjustments (move/zoom) can resolve compositional issues.

sections.title: Removing subjects: clone stamp and rotation fixes
sections.description: Demonstrates removing a person by rotating to align slopes and using clone stamping to seamlessly fill gaps, preserving natural grain and texture.

sections.title: History Paint: non-destructive post-processing workflow
sections.description: Introduces History Paint as a faster, non-destructive method to adjust multiple zones without using many layers, including how to remix edits later.

sections.title: Sky and foreground color grading: whites, color balance, and painting
sections.description: A deep dive into sky adjustments and painting warmth into the scene, using whites, color grading, and luminosity adjustments to balance foreground and sky.

sections.title: Three-zone processing and composition refinement
sections.description: Breakdown of treating image as three zones and using targeted edits (texture/clarity for foreground, sky color grading) plus cropping decisions to enhance composition.

sections.title: Vignette, highlights, and focal emphasis
sections.description: Demonstrates applying a controlled vignette and refining highlights to direct attention toward light-rich areas, including painting the vignette back in for balance.

sections.title: Fog layering for depth: dehaze, blur, and layering
sections.description: Shows how to simulate or enhance fog and distance by layering dehaze and blur, then painting the effect into distant parts for added depth.

sections.title: Wrap-up and viewer takeaway
sections.description: Wraps up with emphasis on a small, repeatable toolset (primarily RAW-based adjustments and a handful of Photoshop tools) and the notion that photography emphasizes print-ready results.

featured_techniques.technique: Camera Raw Whites adjustment to preserve sky detail and recover shadows
Clone Stamp with rotation to align slopes and remove a person
Color grading with luminosity masks and selective color
Fog layering using dehaze and blur for depth
Vignette creation and painting in for edge control
